metaDescription: Five wireless printers that print from iPhone and iPad without drivers, compared on setup, ink system, paper handling and what AirPrint cannot do.
expertTake: The Epson EcoTank ET-2800 is the pick for anyone who prints regularly, because its refillable tanks remove the cartridge problem that costs most owners the most. The Canon TS5320 is the value choice for light printing from a phone. If you print a handful of pages a year, a cheap inkjet that dries out between jobs is a worse buy than a laser or a pay-per-use plan.
introParagraphs: AirPrint is a driverless printing method built into iPhone, iPad and Mac. The device finds a compatible printer on the same network and sends the job directly, so there is no app to install and no driver to update.

That convenience is only as good as the printer behind it. The useful comparison is the ink system, how the paper path handles real documents, and whether the machine keeps working after months of sitting idle.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-2800 wireless supertank all-in-one
products.description:
The ET-2800 swaps cartridges for refillable tanks filled from ink bottles, which removes the mechanism that makes most home inkjets expensive to run. The listing highlights cartridge-free printing and a generous starter supply, and the tank design means cost per page falls sharply once you buy bottles instead of cartridges.

It prints, scans and copies, with a flatbed scanner rather than a document feeder, so it suits single pages and photos instead of stacks. AirPrint support lets an iPhone find it over the network without a driver, which is the whole point of this guide, and the setup is a matter of joining the printer to your Wi-Fi.

Compared with the Canon TS5320, the ET-2800 costs more to buy and runs far cheaper per page, which pays off for a household that prints weekly. Keep it powered and run a page now and then, because any inkjet can clog a nozzle when left idle for months, and fill each tank carefully from the matching bottle, which is keyed to avoid mix-ups.
products.bestFor: Households that print every week and want low running cost.
pros: Refillable tanks cut ink cost per page
cons: Higher purchase price than cartridge models
Nozzles can clog if left unused for months

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS5320 wireless all-in-one with AirPrint

specList.label: Display
specList.value: 1.44 in OLED with LED status bar

products.description:
The TS5320 is a compact household all-in-one with a small OLED display and an LED status bar that shows when it needs attention. It is one of the few listings here that names AirPrint in its title, and it uses two FINE cartridges, one for black and one for color, which keeps replacement simple.

Two-cartridge systems are easy to understand but have a known drawback: when the single color cartridge runs out of one ink, you replace the whole thing. For light printing that is acceptable, since a typical family prints a few pages a week of documents and the occasional photo.

Compared with the TR4720, it drops the document feeder but gains a brighter control display. Compared with the ET-2800, it is cheaper to buy and costlier to run. Treat it as the machine for a student or a small household, and print something every few weeks to keep the nozzles clear.
products.bestFor: Students and light home users who print from a phone.
pros: AirPrint named in the listing title

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR4720 all-in-one with feeder and fax
products.description:
The TR4720 adds an automatic document feeder and a built-in fax to the basic all-in-one, which makes it the paperwork machine of this group. If you scan multi-page forms, tax documents or contracts, a feeder saves you from lifting the lid for every sheet.

It lists a 4 x 6 inch borderless photo in about 65 seconds and a power draw of 7 W while working and 0.8 W on standby. Those are the kind of facts that help you compare, because photo speed and standby power matter more over years than the maximum print resolution.

Compared with the TS5320, it gives up the OLED display and keeps the simple cartridge system, so running cost is similar. If you never fax and rarely scan more than a page, the feeder is wasted; if you work from home and handle forms, it is the feature that justifies the model.
products.bestFor: Home offices that scan multi-page paperwork.
pros: Automatic document feeder for multi-page scans
Built-in fax for the rare need
cons: Fax is of little use to many buyers

products.name: HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e wireless all-in-one with duplex and ADF
products.description:
The OfficeJet Pro 8125e is built more like a small-office machine: automatic two-sided printing, an automatic document feeder and a 225-sheet input tray, so you can load a stack and walk away. The listing also mentions HP software that formats web pages and emails for printing.

For AirPrint use, it joins the network like the others and appears in the print dialog without an app. The caveat is the ecosystem: HP's e-series models are sold into the company's subscription ink program, so read the terms on cartridge use and account requirements before you buy, since those policies can restrict third-party ink.

Compared with the TR4720, it prints faster, holds far more paper and duplexes automatically, at a higher price. Compared with the ET-2800, its per-page cost is higher, but its paper handling is far better. Choose it if you print documents daily and value hands-off duplexing.
products.bestFor: Home offices that print daily and want duplex and a large tray.
cons: Cartridges cost more per page than tanks

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS702a print-only wireless printer, 350-sheet capacity

specList.label: Best use
specList.value: Photo and document printing, no scanning

products.description:
The TS702a is the only single-function printer in this guide: no scanner, no copier, no fax. That simplification buys a 350-sheet plain paper capacity, so you refill the tray rarely, and the listing names AirPrint mobile printing alongside borderless photo support on various paper types and sizes.

For someone who prints from an iPhone and never scans, that makes sense. A scanner adds cost, a lid and a mechanism that can fail, and phone scanning apps now handle most single-page needs. The trade is obvious: if you ever need a copy, you will do it through a phone.

Compared with the TS5320, it carries more paper and drops the scanner. Compared with the ET-2800, it uses cartridges and costs more per page. Keep it in a place where it sees a page now and then, since idle inkjets clog, and use the printer's cleaning cycle sparingly because each cycle consumes ink.
products.bestFor: Phone-first printing of documents and photos with no scanning.
pros: Simpler machine with no scanner to fail

products.name: Brother Work Smart 1360 wireless all-in-one with duplex

specList.label: Cloud
specList.value: Print from and scan to cloud apps

products.description:
The Work Smart 1360 is the compact way to get automatic duplex and a document feeder, with a 20-sheet feeder that handles short stacks of forms. It also prints from and scans to cloud apps such as Google Drive and Dropbox, which is handy if you work on a laptop and a phone at once.

Brother printers support AirPrint, so an iPhone finds it on the home network without a driver, and the same machine works with the maker's own app for scanning. It is smaller than the HP 8125e and holds less paper, which is the trade for the lower price and tidier footprint.

Compared with the TR4720, it duplexes automatically instead of needing manual flips, and compared with the ET-2800, it uses cartridges and costs more per page. Print a page every couple of weeks to keep the head clear, and keep a spare black cartridge on hand because documents use it fastest.
products.bestFor: Small home offices that want duplex without a large machine.
pros: Print from and scan to cloud apps

buyingCriteria.explanation: AirPrint finds printers by Bonjour on the same network and sends jobs without a driver. It handles printing, not scanning or ink-level checks on every model. If your router isolates guests or separates subnets, an iPhone on the guest network will not see the printer. Keep both on one network and check the printer supports AirPrint by name.

The ET-2800 uses refillable tanks, while the Canon TS5320, TR4720 and TS702a and the HP 8125e use cartridges. Cartridge machines cost less to buy and more per page. If you print weekly, the tank system repays the higher price. For a few pages a month, the cheaper machine is fine, as long as you accept the cost of ink.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Choose a feeder only if you need it
buyingCriteria.explanation: The TR4720 and HP 8125e have automatic document feeders, and the TS5320, TS702a and ET-2800 do not. A feeder saves time on multi-page scans and copies, and it adds size and cost. If you scan single receipts, a flatbed or your phone is enough.

Inkjet nozzles dry out when unused. A printer left for months may waste ink on cleaning cycles or fail to print. Print one color page every two weeks, and leave the printer plugged in so it can run its own maintenance. A laser avoids this entirely, though it falls outside this guide.

Some printers, including HP's e-series models like the 8125e, are tied to subscription programs and may restrict cartridge choices or require an account. This affects what you can use and how long the printer stays useful. Read the terms on the listing and the box before you buy.

The TS702a holds 350 sheets and the HP 8125e has a 225-sheet tray, while compact models hold far less. A small tray means more refills. Also check whether the machine duplexes automatically, because manual two-sided printing is slow and frustrating.

howWeEvaluated.title: AirPrint support
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked for listings that name AirPrint or driverless mobile printing, such as the TS5320 and TS702a titles. Models from the same manufacturer families that support it were included.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ink system and running cost
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared tank against cartridge designs. The ET-2800 stands apart with refillable tanks, and the Canon and HP models use cartridges with higher cost per page.

howWeEvaluated.title: Paper handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared tray capacity and duplexing. The TS702a holds 350 sheets and the HP 8125e has a 225-sheet tray with automatic duplex, which suit heavy use. The Brother Work Smart 1360 duplexes automatically with a smaller tray, which places it between the Canon models and the HP.

howWeEvaluated.title: Scanner features
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at flatbed versus feeder scanners and print-only designs. The TR4720 and HP 8125e have feeders, while the TS702a has no scanner at all.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership and idle behavior
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered how each machine copes with months of low use and how its ink program works. Tanks and standby draw figures like the TR4720's 0.8 W mattered here.

cards.label: Tank
cards.text: The Epson ET-2800 uses refillable tanks and bottles. Purchase price is higher but cost per page is much lower. It suits households that print weekly and want to stop buying cartridges.

cards.label: Cartridge
cards.text: The Canon models and the HP 8125e use cartridges. They cost less to buy, are easy to swap and suit occasional use, but each page costs more.

howToChoose.note: Weekly printers should choose tanks; occasional printers should choose cartridges.

howToChoose.subheading: For iPhone and iPad Users Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: AirPrint named by the maker, a model that joins your Wi-Fi band and a driverless setup. Confirm your phone and printer share a network, and avoid guest isolation.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Canon TS5320 and TS702a name AirPrint in their listing titles. The Epson ET-2800 and HP 8125e also work by AirPrint on a shared network.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You print weekly or work from home. The Epson ET-2800 saves on ink and the HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e saves time through duplex and its feeder.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You print rarely. The Canon TS5320 or TS702a cost little, but remember that cartridges are the long-term expense.

maintenance.why: Regular use keeps nozzles from drying out. A single color page is enough. Choose a page with color blocks, which exercises every nozzle.
Many printers run self-maintenance when plugged in. Cutting the power at the wall can leave the print head uncapped.

maintenance.interval: As ink runs low, tank models
maintenance.why: Each bottle matches one tank. Fill slowly and wipe any drips before closing the cap.
Dust and fingerprints show as marks on copies. A dry microfiber cloth is enough.
A new router or network name can drop the printer. Re-join it so AirPrint can find it again.

faq.q: Do I need an app to use AirPrint?
faq.a: No. AirPrint is built into iOS and macOS. Choose Print from the share menu and select the printer, which appears when both are on the same network. Some makers offer apps for extra features like scanning.

faq.q: Why can't my iPhone see the printer?
faq.a: The most common cause is a network mismatch, such as the phone on a guest network or a different band. Put both devices on one network, restart the printer and try again.

faq.q: Is a tank printer worth it for light use?
faq.a: Usually not on price alone, since the higher purchase cost takes years to repay. It is worth it if you print weekly or if you are tired of cartridges drying out. A middle path is a cartridge model with high-yield cartridges, which narrows the cost gap without the tank price.
It depends on the model. Some printers accept compatible cartridges and some restrict them through firmware or program terms. Read the listing and the maker's policy before you buy.

faq.q: Do I need a scanner with a feeder?
faq.a: Only if you scan multi-page documents often. A flatbed handles single pages and photos well, and phone scanning apps cover most one-off needs.

faq.q: How do I stop the ink from drying out?
faq.a: Print a color page every couple of weeks and keep the printer plugged in. If a nozzle clogs, run one cleaning cycle and wait, because repeated cycles waste ink.
